title: Grateful Dead Live at Memorial Coliseum on 1973-06-24
lineage: Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a rough start but improving mix, delivering a solid 1973 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star > Eyes > China Doll sequence and rare Bertha.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture of the June‑24‑1973 Portland concert starts out muddy – a cut in I Know You Rider and an under‑mixed drum kit are evident – but after “They Love Each Other” the mix clears up and the performance shines.  The second set is the real prize, featuring a long Dark Star that segues into Eyes of the World and China Doll, plus a rare early‑’73 Bertha and a loose‑going Sugar that many fans cite as highlights.  Overall the show is solid with an uneven first set but a memorable second half, and the recording, while not pristine, is listenable once EQ is applied.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (especially Dark Star/Eyes/China) and give 4‑5 star ratings, while noting early mix problems that keep the recording from being rated excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early tracks are muddy with a noticeable cut around 2:28 in I Know You Rider and Billy Hart's kit under‑mixed; channels appear reversed on some SBD copies. After the first few songs the mix clears up and becomes very listenable, especially from Dark Star onward.

standout_songs: Dark Star > Eyes of the World > China Doll
poor_songs: Row Jimmy (mixed reception, considered weak by some reviewers)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is uneven with a few flubs and average ‘73 material; the second set solidifies the concert, building to an extended Dark Star jam that carries the show’s momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for special, "perfect" guitar tone on Dark Star and overall strong playing throughout the night.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for a jazzy vamp in Dark Star and brilliant keyboard work on China Cat Sunflower and You Ain't Woman Enough; his improvisation is called “Philo‑Stop” by some reviewers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (keys) noted as amazing on Mexicali Blues, China Cat Sunflower, and other second‑set moments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy Hart's kit is reported as poorly mixed early in the show; otherwise no specific drumming issues mentioned.
